title: Dimensions of a ring and its formal power series ring
summary: Understanding the relation between $\dim R$ and $\dim R[[x]]$ is a classical problem in commutative algebra. For a Noetherian ring $R$, one has $\dim R[[x]]=\dim R+1$, but the general case is considerably more delicate. In 1973, Arnold proved that finite power-series dimension requires the strong finite type (SFT) condition, whereas, in 2002, Coykendall constructed a one-dimensional SFT domain whose power series ring has infinite dimension.
